definition: A general-purpose, interpreted programming language with dynamic typing and a large ecosystem of libraries, used for automation, data analysis, web development, and scientific computing.
An open-source document format and web-based environment that stores a sequence of cells containing executable code, its output, and Markdown narrative, run by a language kernel.
A runtime instance of a class in Python that bundles data and behavior; every value in Python is an object with a type, identity, and methods.
A name bound to an object in memory via assignment with =, which references the current value rather than declaring a fixed type or storage slot.
The core built-in categories for values in Python, commonly int for integers, float for floating-point numbers, str for text, and bool for True/False, inspected with type().
Explicitly creating a value of a different type from an existing value using constructor functions such as int(), float(), str(), and bool().
Non-executing text in source code prefixed with # (or a docstring in triple quotes) that explains intent for readers and is ignored by the interpreter.
A control-flow construct (if, elif, else) that evaluates a condition to a boolean and executes the first branch whose condition is true, with indentation defining each block.
A control-flow construct that repeatedly executes a block, either while a condition remains true (while) or once per element in a sequence (for), with break and continue modifying iteration.
Extracting a substring from a string with bracket notation s[start:stop:step], where indices are zero-based and stop is exclusive, supporting omitted bounds and negative indices.
A formatted string literal prefixed with f that evaluates expressions inside braces at runtime, as in f"{value}" or f"{x:.2f}".
An ordered, mutable sequence type in Python written with square brackets, allowing duplicate elements, indexing, slicing, and methods such as append().
An ordered, immutable sequence type in Python written with parentheses, which can be used as a dictionary key when its elements are hashable and supports unpacking.
A mutable mapping type in Python that stores key–value pairs in braces, provides unique keys, preserves insertion order, and exposes methods like keys(), values(), and items().
An unordered collection type in Python that stores unique hashable elements, supports fast membership testing, and provides set operations such as union, intersection, and difference.
A concise expression of the form [expression for item in iterable if condition] that builds a new list by transforming and optionally filtering elements of an iterable.
A directory of Python modules with an importable namespace, distributed as a library that extends the language with additional functionality installed via a package manager.
A Python package providing the ndarray object for homogeneous, contiguous numeric arrays and vectorized operations implemented in compiled code.
A Python package built on NumPy that provides Series and DataFrame structures for labeled, tabular data manipulation and analysis.
A two-dimensional, labeled tabular data structure in pandas composed of rows and named columns, each column backed by a Series and supporting vectorized operations.
